before.name: Econolite
before.description: Traffic signal controllers, cabinets, and intersection management systems

paragraphs: Econolite sells traffic management equipment and services to transportation agencies responsible for roadway efficiency. The catalog includes traffic control cabinets in standard configurations and to unique specifications. It sells traffic signal controllers for intersection management. Detection sensors cover vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians. The company is also a licensed electrical contractor doing traffic signal and ITS maintenance and repair.

Its cabinet designs draw on features of Caltrans, NEMA and ITS cabinets. The Advanced Traffic Control Cabinet uses high-speed serial communications. Its standard configuration allows up to 32 signal outputs and 120 detection inputs. A separate line covers NEMA TS1 and TS2 cabinets built for traffic applications. Battery backup keeps signals operating during a power disruption.

Agencies can book an on-site session with the company to review cabinet performance and specifications. Recent site news names a distributor for the Northwest United States. It also reports European Union certification for a radar detection product. Another item describes adaptive traffic control in Hamburg with Umovity and PTV Group.

before.name: Handtevy
before.description: Pediatric emergency dosing system and app for EMS agencies - exhibited at FDIC International 2027

paragraphs: Handtevy sells clinical workflow software for emergency medicine, pairing precision dosing and protocol access for clinicians with control and reporting for the administrators who oversee them. The buyers are agencies and hospitals looking to raise their standard of emergency care.

Handtevy Mobile puts precision dosing, real-time protocols, and clinical decision support directly in clinicians' hands. Weight-based calculations are cross-checked against clinical thresholds and customized to local protocols. An admin portal lets administrators manage pharmacology, protocols, order sets, and checklists across an organization and control exactly what clinicians see at the point of care. The software connects directly with ePCR and EHR platforms, which the company says involves no PHI exposure and no IT infrastructure.

The company says it is used by more than 200,000 clinicians in all 50 states. Pediatric Emergency Standards, Inc. has operated under the name Handtevy since 2010, offering evidence-based software to healthcare providers domestically and internationally. Its founder, Dr. Peter Antevy, is a practicing pediatric emergency medicine physician and EMS Medical Director. The company started in pediatrics and now describes its goal as improving emergency care for adults as well.

before.name: Open Point
before.description: Community engagement and stakeholder relationship management platform for councils, transportation agencies, and infrastructure project owners - exhibited at 3CMA 2026

paragraphs: Open Point sells one platform that combines community engagement with stakeholder relationship management. The company states that the platform brings community voices and stakeholder relationships into one place across the project lifecycle. Stakeholder records centralize contact details, project context, relationships, and engagement history in one connected profile.

The platform is sold as two products, Community Engagement and Stakeholder Relationship Management. Social Point by Open Point brings participation tools, visual project pages, and built-in reporting together for running engagement. Engagement tools listed include interactive maps, budget simulations, surveys, polls, and idea boards.

The reporting product processes consultation responses, submissions, emails, transcripts and stakeholder communications. Open Point states that the reporting product is designed for government, infrastructure, utilities, energy and planning organizations. An industries section on the homepage lists Local & State Government among the markets named.

paragraphs: ICC Innovation is the arm of the International Code Council that packages digital tools and software as a service applications for communities. It is offered as an end-to-end suite backed by expert resources.

The lineup includes digital codification tools meant to support safety, compliance and efficiency. A flexible online code experience is offered to raise transparency and efficiency. Content management and process automation route work, requests and notifications so employees and residents can do business from anywhere. Permitting moves online, covering applications, inspection scheduling and application review. Electronic plan review is presented as a secure way to speed up the permit application process.

Training and certification options earn CEUs, LUs or PDHs toward International Code Council certification renewal. The Code Council is steered by a board that meets several times a year to provide oversight and strategic direction. The organization states its mission as building safety. Staff leaders run daily operations for their areas across the family of companies. One address it lists is in Washington, DC.

before.name: Accela
before.description: Permitting, licensing, and code enforcement platform for state and local government - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, ICMA 2026, NRPA 2026, ICC 2026
before.source: ICMA 2025; NRPA 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026; ICC 2026

paragraphs: Accela sells software that government agencies use to run permitting, licensing, and asset management from a single system. Its applications are built for individual government service workflows and can operate together or be deployed only where an agency needs them.

For building departments, intake, plan review, inspections, and permit issuance sit in one workflow rather than in separate disconnected steps. Reviewers from different departments work the same record at once, with annotations and approvals tracked as they happen. Planning teams get the same shared review model, plus automated public notice generation, hearing schedules, and agency notifications. Applicants can see where a case stands and receive consolidated feedback from every reviewing department.

The company says it has thirty years of government expertise built into the product. Testimonials on the site are attributed to municipal staff, including a chief building official in McAllen, Texas. Residents and businesses who encounter Accela through a local agency are directed to that agency rather than to the company.

quote.text: The end-to-end platform for permitting, licensing, asset management and more. Built for high performing agencies.

before.name: Archistar
before.description: AI planning and building code assessment tools sold to councils and cities - exhibited at ICMA 2026, Smart Cities Connect 2026, ICC 2026
before.source: competitor sweep; ICMA 2026; Smart Cities Connect 2026; ICC 2026

paragraphs: Archistar sells AI plan review software to local governments, with a product called AI PreCheck that speeds building code and zoning compliance checks so permits can be issued faster. The same platform is offered to developers, architects and certifiers, who can check compliance before submitting to a municipality or council.

Submitters drag and drop design files onto the platform, which accepts PDF, CAD or BIM formats and reviews them in 2D or 3D. The software then evaluates each submission against the city's local codes and regulations. It is built on generative AI, computer vision and machine learning. Applicants receive standardized reports. For municipalities and councils with particular zoning, planning and compliance requirements, tailored and white-labeled versions are offered.

The company says Archistar was founded by Dr. Benjamin Coorey in 2010 and began life as an education portal. It grew from a university research project into a platform that could read planning rules, run feasibility tests and generate compliant designs in minutes. The site states that Archistar powers digital planning for over 30 cities and governments across Australia, Canada and the United States. Among the municipalities it names supporting are LA County, the City of Los Angeles, the City of Austin and the City of New York. Offices are listed across Los Angeles, Vancouver and Sydney.

paragraphs: Madison AI sells a platform that turns a government's own files and systems into an AI assistant for staff. The pages describe drafting staff reports, looking up code and zoning by parcel, researching voting history, and analyzing contracts against procurement standards. The homepage states that the product makes work easier in local government and water districts.

The site says the engine was created by Washoe County and OnStrategy. The about page names Washoe County as a co-founder and an equity partner rather than only a customer. The site names the City of Reno, Washoe County, and the Northern Nevada Regional Transportation Commission among government clients.

Deployment is described as taking about four weeks, with full deployment in less than sixty days. The homepage says the product is used by 65+ local governments and counting. A time study by the City of Reno is cited as reducing staff report production by more than 75%.

quote.text: Off-the-shelf tools have value, but only purpose-built AI from their data and records can actually tackle the specialized and nuanced work governments complete every day.

provenance.quote: The Madison AI™ engine transform decades of files and disconnected systems into an AI built to support your staff’s knowledge work. Fast, accurate, and cited.
Analyze contracts against procurement standards.
We make work easier in local government and water districts.
The Madison AI™ engine was created by Washoe County and OnStrategy. Why?

Madison AI was co-founded with Washoe County, NV, making them not just a customer, but an equity partner shaping every decision. The result is a platform designed only for local government, by the very people who live its challenges every day.
The Madison AI™ engine has been deployed within the City of Reno, Washoe County, Northern Nevada Regional Transportation Commission, and other government clients.
The Madison AI™ platform’s setup, data science, and deployment can be completed and ready for your team in about four weeks. We can fully deploy in less than sixty days.
Used and trusted by 65+ local governments and counting
In a time study by the City of Reno, the Madison AI™ platform reduced staff report production by more than 75%.

paragraphs: GovWell sells software that city and county governments use to run permitting, licensing, planning, and code enforcement work. Residents and businesses use the same system to reach services, pay, and get answers outside office hours.

Permits, plan review, and inspections are handled together in one place for staff. Licensing runs online too, with applicants filing, paying, and renewing while staff keep records and approvals on their side. Code enforcement officers track cases, schedule inspections, and follow issues to closure. The company argues that AI can do real work in these processes, reviewing applications against local code, answering resident questions, flagging violations in plans, and routing inspections.

GovWell says it was founded by the son of a general contractor who watched his father struggle to get permits quickly. Its case for existing is that local governments cannot hire software engineers at competitive salaries. Deployment strategists and configuration tooling are meant to shorten implementations against older systems.

quote.text: Then you try to file a building permit.

before.name: Accela
before.description: Permitting, licensing, and code enforcement platform for state and local government - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, ICMA 2026, NRPA 2026, ICC 2026, APA California Chapter 2026
before.source: ICMA 2025; NRPA 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026; ICC 2026; APA California Chapter 2026

paragraphs: Accela sells software that government agencies use to run permitting, licensing, and asset management from a single system. Its applications are built for individual government service workflows and can operate together or be deployed only where an agency needs them.

For building departments, intake, plan review, inspections, and permit issuance sit in one workflow rather than in separate disconnected steps. Reviewers from different departments work the same record at once, with annotations and approvals tracked as they happen. Planning teams get the same shared review model, plus automated public notice generation, hearing schedules, and agency notifications. Applicants can see where a case stands and receive consolidated feedback from every reviewing department.

The company says it has thirty years of government expertise built into the product. Testimonials on the site are attributed to municipal staff, including a chief building official in McAllen, Texas. Residents and businesses who encounter Accela through a local agency are directed to that agency rather than to the company.

quote.text: The end-to-end platform for permitting, licensing, asset management and more. Built for high performing agencies.

paragraphs: SwiftGov is presented as an AI-native operating system for local government, built to strengthen permit and plan review, compliance, knowledge, data, and service delivery. The platform automates intake processing, flags potential code conflicts before they become resubmittals, and standardizes reviewer comments. The products listed for the Hernando County engagement are SwiftGov, Development Services Transformation, GIS Services, and Swift Analytics.

The jurisdictions named on the SwiftGov page are Hernando County, Pasco County, Clay County, Walton County, City of Jacksonville, City of Titusville, and Hernando County Clerk of Court, all in Florida. The case studies page describes municipal development services teams using SwiftGov for regulatory review. The case study ties the deployment to the rebuild surge after Hurricane Helene and Hurricane Milton in 2024.

Initial plan review time at Hernando County is reported as 30 days to 15 minutes, a 93% reduction in single-family home zoning review times. The county estimates direct net savings of $1.5 million annually across four primary areas, including reduced reliance on temporary staff and third-party plan review.

before.name: GovWell
before.description: AI permitting and licensing platform: 24/7 resident assistant, AI code-compliance review - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, Maryland Municipal League 2026, ICC 2026, APA Colorado Chapter 2026
before.source: ICMA 2025; NACo 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026; Maryland Municipal League 2026; ICC 2026; APA Colorado Chapter 2026

paragraphs: GovWell sells software that city and county governments use to run permitting, licensing, planning, and code enforcement work. Residents and businesses use the same system to reach services, pay, and get answers outside office hours.

Permits, plan review, and inspections are handled together in one place for staff. Licensing runs online too, with applicants filing, paying, and renewing while staff keep records and approvals on their side. Code enforcement officers track cases, schedule inspections, and follow issues to closure. The company argues that AI can do real work in these processes, reviewing applications against local code, answering resident questions, flagging violations in plans, and routing inspections.

GovWell says it was founded by the son of a general contractor who watched his father struggle to get permits quickly. Its case for existing is that local governments cannot hire software engineers at competitive salaries. Deployment strategists and configuration tooling are meant to shorten implementations against older systems.

paragraphs: ICC Innovation is the arm of the International Code Council that packages digital tools and software as a service applications for communities. It is offered as an end-to-end suite backed by expert resources.

The lineup includes digital codification tools meant to support safety, compliance and efficiency. A flexible online code experience is offered to raise transparency and efficiency. Content management and process automation route work, requests and notifications so employees and residents can do business from anywhere. Permitting moves online, covering applications, inspection scheduling and application review. Electronic plan review is presented as a secure way to speed up the permit application process.

Training and certification options earn CEUs, LUs or PDHs toward International Code Council certification renewal. The Code Council is steered by a board that meets several times a year to provide oversight and strategic direction. The organization states its mission as building safety. Staff leaders run daily operations for their areas across the family of companies. One address it lists is in Washington, DC.

paragraphs: OpenGov sells a cloud platform for cities, counties, and state agencies that connects budgeting, finance, permitting, and asset management in one system. The Public Service Platform brings ERP and Community Operations products together, spanning Financial Management, Budgeting & Performance, Procurement & Contract Management, Permitting & Licensing, 311 Request Management, Utility Billing, and Payroll. OG Assist is the AI assistant built into every product, helping staff find answers, draft documents, and complete guided actions across the platform.

Software is built specifically for cities, counties, and state agencies, and the pages say over 2,000 governments run day-to-day operations on it. The buyers named are cities, counties, townships, special districts, school districts, utilities, and state agencies across the United States. Compliance controls built in cover GASB, FEMA, HUD, ARPA, and FLSA, and the platform is stated to be SOC 2 compliant.

OpenGov states 4,500+ government software implementations completed, with timelines that vary by product and organizational complexity, typically ranging from 3 to 6 months. Government App Builder is a no-code platform that lets IT teams build custom forms, workflows, and citizen-facing apps, with permissions, audit logs, and version history.

paragraphs: GovWell sells software that city and county governments use to run permitting, licensing, planning, and code enforcement work. Residents and businesses use the same system to reach services, pay, and get answers outside office hours.

Permits, plan review, and inspections are handled together in one place for staff. Licensing runs online too, with applicants filing, paying, and renewing while staff keep records and approvals on their side. Code enforcement officers track cases, schedule inspections, and follow issues to closure. The company argues that AI can do real work in these processes, reviewing applications against local code, answering resident questions, flagging violations in plans, and routing inspections.

GovWell says it was founded by the son of a general contractor who watched his father struggle to get permits quickly. Its case for existing is that local governments cannot hire software engineers at competitive salaries. Deployment strategists and configuration tooling are meant to shorten implementations against older systems.

quote.text: Then you try to file a building permit.

paragraphs: Esri builds ArcGIS, its geographic information system software for mapping and spatial analysis. The company describes itself as the global market leader in GIS software, location intelligence, and mapping. Its stated audience is business, government, and society.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

paragraphs: Via sells software and operating services for public transportation, working with the agencies and cities that run it. The company says it works with more than 700 partners around the world, from rural counties to large transit agencies.

Its on demand microtransit is pitched for first and last mile connections and for places with little transit service. For paratransit, the system optimizes routes and taps other accessible modes when they fit. An eligibility tool automates paratransit applications, approvals, and renewals. A planning product, Remix, is for visualizing data and testing network concepts before a redesign goes live. A student transit product provides scheduling and routing software meant to get every student to school on time.

Via also runs service itself under what it calls a transportation as a service model, rather than only supplying software. Its site carries comments from riders, mayors, agency leaders, planners, and dispatchers. A newer offering, Via Intelligence, is described as giving city and agency leaders recommendations and automations to lift efficiency and service performance.

paragraphs: Accela sells software that government agencies use to run permitting, licensing, and asset management from a single system. Its applications are built for individual government service workflows and can operate together or be deployed only where an agency needs them.

For building departments, intake, plan review, inspections, and permit issuance sit in one workflow rather than in separate disconnected steps. Reviewers from different departments work the same record at once, with annotations and approvals tracked as they happen. Planning teams get the same shared review model, plus automated public notice generation, hearing schedules, and agency notifications. Applicants can see where a case stands and receive consolidated feedback from every reviewing department.

The company says it has thirty years of government expertise built into the product. Testimonials on the site are attributed to municipal staff, including a chief building official in McAllen, Texas. Residents and businesses who encounter Accela through a local agency are directed to that agency rather than to the company.

paragraphs: GovWell sells software that city and county governments use to run permitting, licensing, planning, and code enforcement work. Residents and businesses use the same system to reach services, pay, and get answers outside office hours.

Permits, plan review, and inspections are handled together in one place for staff. Licensing runs online too, with applicants filing, paying, and renewing while staff keep records and approvals on their side. Code enforcement officers track cases, schedule inspections, and follow issues to closure. The company argues that AI can do real work in these processes, reviewing applications against local code, answering resident questions, flagging violations in plans, and routing inspections.

GovWell says it was founded by the son of a general contractor who watched his father struggle to get permits quickly. Its case for existing is that local governments cannot hire software engineers at competitive salaries. Deployment strategists and configuration tooling are meant to shorten implementations against older systems.

paragraphs: SwiftGov is presented as an AI-native operating system for local government, built to strengthen permit and plan review, compliance, knowledge, data, and service delivery. The platform automates intake processing, flags potential code conflicts before they become resubmittals, and standardizes reviewer comments. The products listed for the Hernando County engagement are SwiftGov, Development Services Transformation, GIS Services, and Swift Analytics.

The jurisdictions named on the SwiftGov page are Hernando County, Pasco County, Clay County, Walton County, City of Jacksonville, City of Titusville, and Hernando County Clerk of Court, all in Florida. The case studies page describes municipal development services teams using SwiftGov for regulatory review. The case study ties the deployment to the rebuild surge after Hurricane Helene and Hurricane Milton in 2024.

Initial plan review time at Hernando County is reported as 30 days to 15 minutes, a 93% reduction in single-family home zoning review times. The county estimates direct net savings of $1.5 million annually across four primary areas, including reduced reliance on temporary staff and third-party plan review.

paragraphs: GovWell sells software that city and county governments use to run permitting, licensing, planning, and code enforcement work. Residents and businesses use the same system to reach services, pay, and get answers outside office hours.

Permits, plan review, and inspections are handled together in one place for staff. Licensing runs online too, with applicants filing, paying, and renewing while staff keep records and approvals on their side. Code enforcement officers track cases, schedule inspections, and follow issues to closure. The company argues that AI can do real work in these processes, reviewing applications against local code, answering resident questions, flagging violations in plans, and routing inspections.

GovWell says it was founded by the son of a general contractor who watched his father struggle to get permits quickly. Its case for existing is that local governments cannot hire software engineers at competitive salaries. Deployment strategists and configuration tooling are meant to shorten implementations against older systems.

quote.text: Then you try to file a building permit.

paragraphs: Social Explorer sells a subscription web application for community analysis, built so that data is acquired and processed before the customer arrives. The application couples a data library with an AI-enabled Data Navigator that takes natural-language questions and returns dataset-specific analysis. Output takes the form of maps, charts, tables, and reports, and data can be exported to Excel, CSV, PDF, PNG, SAS, or SPSS formats.

The mapping product, SE Research, covers location-based community data at every geographic level and is positioned for users without a data science background. A subscription includes a library of crime, demographic, economic, environmental, equity, health, housing, political, and transportation data drawn from public and private sources.

SE Transform, a data pipeline management product, launches as a managed service and is built on Apache Airflow infrastructure. SE AI is sold as a domain-specific data chat interface, with a conversational front end, an API layer, and an admin panel. The homepage says the customer base includes educational and research institutions, government agencies, non-profits, healthcare systems, and businesses.

quote.text: Most of the time spent on community analysis involves acquiring and processing data.

provenance.quote: Get instant access to all the community data you need through one integrated application.
Prompt our AI-enabled Data Navigator with a general question using natural language and get dataset-specific analysis in minutes.
Export data to Excel, CSV, PDF, PNG, SAS, or SPSS formats.
Our demographic mapping software is designed to make demographic data accessible to everyone who wants to be data-driven.

Every subscription to SE Research comes with access to our vast library of structured crime, demographic, economic, environmental, equity, health, housing, political, and transportation data assembled from dozens of reputable public and private sources.
SE Transform launches as a managed service combining expert data engineering with platform technology.
Instead of navigating complex menus or writing SQL, they ask questions in plain English.
We help hundreds of educational and research institutions, government agencies, non-profits, healthcare systems, and businesses understand their communities every day.

before.source: research pass: HHS conference exhibitor research 2026-08-25; AIRA 2026

paragraphs: Strategic Solutions Group sells public health software applications for state and local agencies, built on a case management platform called Casetivity. The applications named on the site cover electronic disease surveillance, immunization information systems, lead poisoning prevention, early intervention and vital records. Delivery is described as cloud enabled, fully managed and sold on subscription.

The disease surveillance product ingests ELR and eCR data in real time and handles lab data management, including susceptibility, sequencing and negative findings. Pages for it claim coverage of 90+ reportable conditions. The same pages state that the product is HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified.
The immunization system page addresses state health departments and public health agencies. That page points to an implementation in the State of Massachusetts.

quote.text: SSG’s overall mission is to support public sector organizations with IT solutions that enhance the services delivered to residents.

provenance.quote: SSG offers public health software applications for state and local agencies looking to modernize workflows, reduce administrative burden, and improve program performance.

SSG offers a suite of fit-to-purpose applications built on its Casetivity platform, including Electronic Disease Surveillance, Immunization Information System (IIS), Lead Poisoning Prevention, and Early Intervention Part C Data System.
Cloud enabled, worry free, fully managed, subscription solution
Real-time ELR and eCR ingestion with advanced lab data management, including susceptibility, sequencing, and negative findings.
Covers 90+ reportable conditions
HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, with MFA, role-based access, and full data encryption in transit and at rest.

State health departments and public health agencies need faster, more reliable ways to manage immunization records, reduce manual work, adapt to changing needs and improve response achieve sustainability.
Successful implementation in the State of Massachusetts.

paragraphs: POM sells parking meters and dates the first parking meter installed in Oklahoma City to 1935. Meters are manufactured at a woman-owned, ISO-certified facility in Russellville, Arkansas. The meters use a power management chip, a low-power modem, and a memory LCD graphic display.

All POM parking meters can be programmed to accept prepaid smart chip cards, alone or in conjunction with coins. The card is a ParkCard, sized to fit into a pocket or wallet. MeterManager.net has a smart card management module that uses a USB card reader and writer interface. That module lets the parking system administrator issue smartcards and add value to depleted cards.

It is the cooperative arm of PPA, the analogue of NASPO ValuePoint, not a software vendor like OpenGov or Bonfire. paragraphs: NIRA Dynamics sells Tire Pressure Indicator, software that determines tire inflation pressure from wheel speed signals instead of in-wheel sensors. Vehicle Assistance, Driver Support and Road Maintenance are the three areas the product collection is presented under. Winter Road Insights is offered to road owners and operators as connected vehicle data for winter maintenance. Road Health is described as an automated system for road monitoring that uses connected vehicle data to lower operational costs.

Car manufacturers are named as one group the products are meant to serve, alongside road maintenance. The company describes itself as a supplier with certifications such as TISAX, ISO 9001, Automotive SPICE and AUTOSAR.

paragraphs: LLMC is a nonprofit library consortium that provides access to global legal and historical documents through its database. The organization was founded in 1976 as a nonprofit cooperative of libraries dedicated to preserving legal and government materials. Early work used microform, and LLMC supplied libraries with reproductions of aging and at-risk legal collections.

The LLMC Digital database launched in 2003 and expanded access to rare legal titles including historical statutes, session laws, judicial decisions, administrative regulations, and government reports. Source types in the archive include Attorney General Publications, House & Senate Journals, and Treaties & Arbitrations. Special collections named on the site include the Yale Blackstone Collection, the Drew Days III Archive, and Early State Records.

The collection is described as a resource for students, historians, researchers, attorneys, and scholars. Access runs through a member portal, and an Open Access collection is offered to the public. LLMC works in partnership with hundreds of libraries and institutions to identify, preserve, and digitize historic, legal, and governmental records.

paragraphs.text: Kapsch TrafficCom sells tolling and traffic management technology, set out on its own page as a portfolio of ITS, or intelligent transportation system, technologies.
paragraphs.quote: Kapsch TrafficCom zählt zu den erfolgreichsten Technologie­unternehmen Österreichs mit globaler Präsenz. Mit seinem Portfolio an ITS (Intelligent Transportation System)-Technologien schafft das Unternehmen innovative Lösungen für nachhaltige Mobilität, um Staubildung zu vermeiden und die Umwelt zu schützen.

paragraphs.quote: Die spanische Stadt León modernisiert ihr Verkehrsmanagement mit Kapsch TrafficCom

paragraphs.text: The same page counts realised projects in more than 50 countries.
paragraphs.quote: realisierte Projekte in mehr als 50 Ländern

paragraphs.text: Another item reports a toll transponder plant in Mississauga, Ontario.
paragraphs.quote: Kapsch TrafficCom hat in Nordamerika einen weiteren bedeutenden Produktionsmeilenstein erreicht: Mittlerweile sind 115 Millionen Mauttransponder am Standort des Unternehmens in Mississauga, Ontario vom Band gelaufen.

before.name: Autura
before.description: Towing lifecycle software for city towing programs and impound management (ex-AutoReturn + TSD)

paragraphs: Autura sells software to the people who handle towing on public roads, from the officers and dispatchers who order a tow to the impound teams who store and release the vehicle. The company says it supplies towing management and unclaimed vehicle auction software to public safety agency leaders and towing and recovery business owners.

On the agency side, the product handles tow requests and rotation, and Autura says it gives agencies complete control over their towing program. Impound work is pulled into a single compliant system covering storage lookup, regulated fees, and lien and notification workflows. Lien handling uses state-approved lien search and notification capabilities. A separate marketplace covers how impound facilities sell unclaimed vehicles. Agencies can also see private tows logged in their jurisdiction.

The company took its current shape after a 2024 merger with TRAXERO and other acquisitions. It says many of its team members are former tow operators, impound managers, law enforcement officers, and telecommunicators. Its stated reason for the work is roadside safety.

before.name: CaseWorthy
before.description: Case management and HMIS for government-funded human services programs

paragraphs: CaseWorthy sells a software platform for case and program management in human services. Its buyers are nonprofit organizations and local and state governments that deliver social care programs.

The platform pulls programs, people, data and workflows together in one system rather than scattering them across separate tools. Agencies configure their own workflows, forms, assessments and service plans to match how each program operates. Reporting for funders is built into the platform instead of assembled in spreadsheets. Underneath sits a data lakehouse called CORE that consolidates information from CaseWorthy applications and outside sources. CORE ships baseline data models for particular sectors, including HMIS for homeless services, aging services and workforce development metrics.

Beyond case management there are applications for HCBS and I/DD providers covering care coordination, scheduling and Medicaid-supported service delivery. Another handles scheduling, documentation and billing for Home and Community-Based Services agencies. An AI copilot named Cara is embedded in the platform to reduce documentation time and surface insights. The company states that the organizations it serves touch more than 41% of the US population.

paragraphs: DZS sells broadband network equipment and software to network operators, with the portfolio presented on the site under the Zhone name and spanning broadband access, mobile, optical and home edge products. The site also pitches electric cooperatives and utilities on bringing broadband to the communities they serve.

On the access side, the company describes an evolution from XGS-PON toward 50G PON and beyond. Its Xtreme Access software manages the access service chain from customer premise equipment through optical network elements to the edge of the internet. That software is meant to run third-party gear as well, including gateways, OLTs, switches and BNGs. A separate fiber extension line uses Gfast over copper already in place to deliver fiber-like speeds where the last hop is hard to build. Those distribution point units can be reverse powered from a network termination device inside the home.

Buyers are addressed as operators capitalizing on government and private investor funded multi-gigabit broadband rollouts. Company news on the home page includes the opening of a research and development center in Hanoi, Vietnam. Its blog index writes about middle-mile networks for utilities and electric cooperatives.

before.name: Dimonoff
before.description: Streetlight control nodes and SCMS smart-city management platform for municipalities and utilities - exhibited at Smart Cities Connect 2026

paragraphs: Dimonoff sells smart street lighting control, connecting street and commercial lighting to a single platform so teams can monitor every fixture in real time. The site dates its work in smart street lighting control back to 2006.

A controller fits a NEMA or Zhaga socket on any LED fixture, from any manufacturer, and dims over 0-10V or DALI. The nodes network over Wi-SUN, RF mesh or LTE-M, and keep running their schedule if the link drops. In the office, one interface holds groups, schedules, dimming profiles, faults and reports, and pushes work orders into the asset system a city already runs. The platform also manages nodes from third-party manufacturers, so hardware from a previous supplier does not have to be scrapped. One part number covers supply voltages from 110 to 480 Vac nominal at 50/60 Hz. Node firmware is updated over the air rather than by a crew in a truck.

Networks already running on the platform account for more than 219,500 connected endpoints, by the company's count. Dimonoff states that all of its hardware and software is designed, developed, manufactured and supported in North America. The support FAQ names Groupe Vectanor as the parent company and says it joined the Wi-SUN Alliance as a Contributing Member in April 2026.

OD Security North America, a Women-Owned Small Business, is the North American Distributor of the SOTER RS Full Body Security Scanning System, and strategic R&D partner to OD Security BV.
OD Security BV, a leading entity within the specialist technology and engineering sector of SMI Group, has accumulated over 60 years of experience in the design and manufacturing of state-of-the-art Medical and Security X-Ray Equipment.

before.name: Beacon by Trek Medics
before.description: Mobile-phone-based emergency dispatch and responder coordination software for EMS, fire, disaster response, and alternative crisis response teams - exhibited at NatCon 2026

paragraphs: Beacon is dispatch software from Trek Medics International that lets a responder organization alert, track and coordinate its people using ordinary mobile phones.

A dispatcher creates an agency account on the web, adds responders, and invites them to install the mobile app. Incidents then go out to those responders by web, mobile and text message. It carries GPS tracking and reporting, and can either connect to an existing computer-aided dispatch system or stand in where a call center has to be built from nothing. The app needs iOS 16 or Android 7 to run the current version.

Ambulance services, fire departments, disaster response teams and search and rescue teams use it in more than 20 countries. Alternative response networks also use it to send community responders to mental health emergencies, overdoses and domestic violence calls. The organization offers a 90-day free trial.

before.name: Can/Am Technologies
before.description: Teller enterprise cashiering, receipting and online payment software for city, county and state finance and treasury departments - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: Can/Am Technologies sells Teller, a cashiering and point-of-sale package made for local and state government agencies across North America. More than 80 state and local governments use it for cashiering, payment technology, and credit processing. The idea is a single hub that centralizes revenue collection, credit processing, and reconciliation.

Residents pay through web and mobile portals, which clear through a processor cloud. Departments that collect revenue submit structured batches directly instead of handing paper to a cashier to re-key. Lockbox files, third-party systems, and online application payments import automatically on a schedule the agency sets. At the close of business Teller posts a single organized general ledger entry while accounts receivable stays in sync. It also produces the ICL file carrying scanned check images and MICR data so checks clear electronically.

The stated audience is state and local governments, education, and utilities. The company cites over 20 years of experience in those markets. Teller integrates with financials, accounts receivable, tax, parking, and records systems. Every modification to a payment, session, or batch is recorded and shown as an audit timeline.

paragraphs: SOLUS develops digital products for libraries of all sizes, from local branches to library consortiums. Three of the products offered are The Library App, eb#1, and LUCi, which the company describes as working together. The Library App is described as giving patrons mobile access to borrowing, reservations, events, and notifications.

LUCi is the discovery platform and website, uniting catalogue search, account management, events, and content. paragraphs: ViaPath Technologies sells technology to correctional facilities, aimed at helping them operate more safely and effectively. The people it serves are incarcerated and formerly incarcerated individuals, their families, and the corrections sector.

The product line covers phones, tablets, video, digital mail, and payments. Alongside it sits a security and intelligence layer built on AI-driven threat detection across calls, messages, and digital activity. There are also programs and training tools meant to prepare incarcerated individuals for employment after release. The company frames the whole of it as an effort to reduce recidivism through reentry support, facility management, and reliable communication.

ViaPath is headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, and says it supports over 2,300 correctional facilities across North America, the UK, and Australia. Its home page claims more than 30 years providing offender management solutions and over a million global users. The stated offering spans secure digital communications, educational tools, payment processing, and data intelligence.

paragraphs: Axon sells public safety agencies a connected set of hardware and software: Axon Body 4 cameras, Axon Fleet 3 cameras, TASER 10 energy weapons and drones, unified on a real-time crime center platform with an open ecosystem of integrated partners. The company describes itself as an operating system for public safety. TASER 10, its current less-lethal weapon, can deploy up to 10 individually targeted probes without reloading when de-escalation fails.

Axon Fusus puts officer location, alerts, dispatch data, ALPR overlays and video feeds on a single live map so command, field and real-time crime center teams work from the same picture. Residents and businesses can opt in through Community Connect to share their camera video, and those cameras then appear on the Fusus map. The Axon AI Era Plan bundles current and future Axon AI products for a fixed annual cost. Among them is Draft One, which generates first-draft report narratives from audio transcripts of digital evidence and details the officer narrates. Axon Assistant, a voice assistant on the Body 4 camera, translates conversations when no human interpreter is available.

Chief Gary Berg of Campbell PD is quoted saying Fusus lets him see live location, alerts and video from body cams, drones and public safety cameras in one platform. Axon says it is on a mission to cut gun-related deaths between police and the public in half by 2033 through technology, training and trust.

paragraphs: SAND builds Symmetri, which it describes as a control layer for the infrastructure systems a society depends on. The company presents it as a single operating system for managing and controlling complex infrastructure, meant to be deployed at scale in weeks. The sectors it names are government, water, energy, telecom, and healthcare.

SAND says the platform is running in more than 18 countries across those sectors with no mission-critical failures. Three groups are meant to work in a deployment at once. Data engineers and MLOps teams tune models, build pipelines, and ship applications on top of Symmetri. Front-line staff such as grid controllers and water utility operators act on its outputs in real time. Program directors and policy leaders use its consequence models to set strategy and allocate resources.

The site lists production programs it attributes to operators around the world. One connects rural clinics into a single network serving millions of patients. Another reports roughly 19,000 structures assessed and about $0.8B in losses prioritized across affected wards.

before.name: Diversified Computer Services (DCS)
before.description: CIMS work order, asset and daily task management software for county road, highway and public works departments - exhibited at NACE 2026

paragraphs: Diversified Computer Services sells information management software used by local governments to run daily operations. Its main product for that market is CIMS, which offers more than 25 functional modules for local government departments. The company says it has been helping local governments capture and manage information for more than 30 years.

CIMS centralizes and automates the creation, assignment, and tracking of tasks, projects, and work orders. Every functional module is made available to all customers, so enhancements reach the whole user community. Integrated mapping generates interactive maps based on Google Maps without specialist operators. More than 500 dynamic reports let departments measure performance and study trends. In the field, problems can be reported and converted into work orders, with GPS coordinates captured and photos uploaded.

Alongside CIMS the company sells TracSpot, GPS tracking software used by businesses and local governments for situational awareness. A facilities management system tracks work orders start to finish and shows where funds go through budget and purchase tracking. Ongoing training and support come with the standard subscription. Customers also get an invitation to an annual user conference.

before.name: CityView
before.description: Community development, permitting and inspections software for municipalities

paragraphs: CityView sells community development software to municipalities, giving them one integrated system for permitting, inspections, planning, code enforcement and licensing. The company describes the platform as purpose-built for local government.

Permits run their full lifecycle in one system, with electronic plans review, mobile field access and automated workflows configured to a jurisdiction's own rules rather than a generic template. Planning teams track rezoning, subdivision, variance and development applications through review, referral and public hearing. Complaints and enforcement cases connect to the same permits and property data. Licensing covers business licenses, cannabis permits, short-term rentals and animal licenses, with online applications, automated renewals and fee calculation. Residents and contractors submit applications, schedule inspections and pay online at any hour.

The company has focused on software for local governments since 1982. It calls that platform one of the first community development and permitting software platforms in North America. The about page says the business was founded by former local government employees for local government. CityView is part of Harris Computer Systems and Constellation Software Inc. One customer story describes the Town of Bradford West Gwillimbury, Ontario, moving to a fully electronic plan review process while upgrading its CityView technology.

paragraphs: IKE sells data acquisition and structural analysis software for power and communication infrastructure. IKE Device speeds up field data collection, and field data uploads to IKE Office Pro for management of pole records. IKE PoleForeman is a structural analysis tool for NESC compliance and pole loading analysis of overhead infrastructure.

The company names utilities, engineering firms, and communications companies among the industries it serves. The about page describes the business as a platform technology company for utility poles and the equipment and services they support. The same page ties those solutions to designing, constructing, and inspecting distribution assets, and to grid resiliency and fiber broadband expansions.

IKE also offers NESC and OSHA training courses for utility and communications workers. The about page lists 500+ enterprise customers across utilities, telecom, and engineering. The same page reports coverage in all 50 states, supporting critical infrastructure nationwide.

quote.text: We help utilities, telecommunication companies, and engineering firms design, manage, and optimize critical overhead infrastructure.

provenance.quote: Delivering actionable insights on power and communication infrastructure with advanced pole data and structural analysis
Speed up field data collection and enhance data quality with IKE Device. Seamlessly upload field data to IKE Office Pro for collaborative management of pole records.
Ensure NESC compliance and accurate pole loading analysis of your overhead infrastructure.
IKE empowers utilities, engineering firms, and communications companies to efficiently acquire and analyze pole data and get actionable insights needed to maintain overhead infrastructure.
We're a platform technology company for utility poles and the critical equipment and services they support.

Our data acquisition and analysis solutions transform how to design, construct, and inspect distribution assets and help achieve critical industry objectives, such as grid resiliency and fiber broadband expansions.
Our courses simplify the complex Code and offer practical insights for utility and communications workers.
Enterprise customers across utilities, telecom, and engineering
Supporting critical infrastructure nationwide

before.name: Pani Energy
before.description: AI performance software for water treatment and desalination operators

paragraphs: Pani Energy is a global software company focused on utility and industrial water and wastewater operations intelligence. Its offering is described as one platform holding a complete intelligence toolbox for a plant. An agent called Agent Zed is described as an AI process engineer that does analysis, answers questions, and performs recurring jobs.

The software works with SCADA data, spreadsheets, paper logs, and plant documents, and can ingest data from a system like Hach WIMS. The company says its team supports operators across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific. Applications are grouped by plant type: wastewater, drinking water, industrial, food and beverage, desalination, and reuse.

The case studies page describes real deployments and what each plant needed, what Pani did, and what it was worth. Entries include a 280 MLD municipal wastewater plant in Washington State and a county water treatment plant in Washington State. Other entries name a beverage bottling plant in Asia and a groundwater replenishment system in California.
